text: This lesson covers writing a platform incident postmortem — the document that actually prevents a resolved incident from happening again.

A postmortem is a structured record with four real components: a factual timeline of what happened, the actual root cause, how it was genuinely resolved, and concrete prevention follow-up with real owners and deadlines. Skip any one of those four and the document stops being useful.

Root cause is not the same thing as the symptom. Response times tripling for 45 minutes is a symptom. An unoptimized Business Rule running a GlideRecord query against every Incident record update, with no indexed filter, consuming semaphores faster than they could be released — that's a root cause. A postmortem that stops at the symptom is really just restating the original complaint with more words. Getting to the real root cause is exactly the work Lesson 19's triage sequence was built for — confirming scope, checking the deployment timeline, and checking resource exhaustion produce the specific chain of cause and effect the postmortem needs.

Prevention actions need owners and deadlines, not good intentions. We'll be more careful with deployments going forward commits nobody to anything. A real prevention action names a specific change, a specific owner, and a specific deadline — that specificity is what turns a postmortem into a document that actually changes the process.

A genuinely useful postmortem is blameless — it focuses on what in the process or system allowed the incident to happen, not on which individual happened to be at the keyboard. This isn't a soft-skills courtesy. If people expect to be blamed, they stop volunteering details, which slows down the investigation a postmortem depends on.

This principle carries over directly from Course 10's Security Incident Response and from general site-reliability engineering culture: the goal is a system that fails less often, not a search for who to blame. Next up: a full incident response lab, working through triage, a support decision, and a real postmortem end to end.
